title: Derive the Z combinator
description: This runnable derivation separates factorial logic from self-application until only a general recursion combinator remains.

steps.description: The comments show why a directly named recursive lambda cannot be written. step1 receives itself as an ordinary argument and uses self(self) for recursion.
step1c rewrites the same idea in curried form, applying self to itself before supplying n.
step2 names the recursive call rec, so the inner factorial body reads rec(n - 1).
fact_gen now contains only factorial logic with rec as its parameter. step3 supplies rec through self-application machinery.

steps.question: What remains after abstracting over fact_gen in step 4?
steps.answer: The result is Z, a combinator that knows nothing about factorials.

steps.description: Z abstracts the self-application pattern over any generator f, then applies it to fact_gen.
fib_gen and sum_gen provide other non-recursive generators. The final calls show Z supplies recursion to both.
